Tier 8 — Developer, Manager & Statistics Dashboard

Real multi-tenancy: a library connects its own catalog, uploads its own documents, and sees its own usage — all through a dashboard, no code changes.

Budget · $0 at pilot scalerev. 2026-07-08
👥

This is the first tier that introduces real accounts — for library staff, not patrons. Every prior tier deliberately avoided a database because nothing needed one; a per-library dashboard genuinely does. Patron-facing behavior across Tiers 1–7 is completely unaffected.

Card 33

Key decisions

Multi-tenancy → Pinecone namespaces

Why: Pinecone's own recommended pattern — physical isolation, independent scaling, clean offboarding. Already the shape of the code: pinecone-scripts already has NAMESPACE = "ns1". How: parameterize it to library_id everywhere.

Tenant data → Supabase

Why: one free-tier service instead of three — Postgres + Auth + Storage together, with Row-Level Security scoping every query to the logged-in staff member's library. How: a libraries table, RLS on auth.uid().

Statistics → query Logfire, don't rebuild it

Why: Tier 1 Phase 4 already instruments every tool call and error. How: tag spans with library_id; dashboard charts are SQL against Logfire's Query API.

Catalog → pluggable connector, Koha first

Why: "their own records" means real ILS integration. Koha is open-source with a documented REST API and realistic for a demo library to actually have. How: a CatalogConnector interface; Open Library stays the default.

Developer surface → keys + the API you have

Why: FastAPI already generates /docs for free. How: extend Tier 6's data-library allowlist into a real revocable API key; link, don't rebuild, the docs.

Dashboard → a protected route, not a new app

Why: same "one component library" principle as every prior tier. How: /admin in the Tier 4 app, gated by Supabase Auth, first tier to need client-side routing.

Card 34

Architecture

Card 35

What it looks like

Mockups, not screenshots — nothing here is built yet. Dashboard chrome, not the chat widget's glow: this is a workspace, not a floating bubble.

Overview — free-tier headroom for Groq/Pinecone/Render surfaced where staff will see it, not buried in a planning doc.

Documents — upload, and a status per document so staff can tell at a glance what made it into their namespace.

Catalog connector — the actual "hookup": Koha's base URL and API key, with a live test-connection result before saving.

Card 38

Definition of done

  • Staff see only their own library's data — enforced by RLS, not UI hiding.
  • A librarian can upload a policy document and have it searchable in chat, in their own namespace, no code changes.
  • A librarian can point catalog search at their real Koha instance instead of Open Library.
  • A stats view shows real usage — volume, tool breakdown, error rate, free-tier headroom — sourced from Logfire.
  • Patron-facing behavior across Tiers 1–7 is completely unaffected.

From here, Tier 9 covers the patron side: real accounts, optional and additive, built on the CatalogConnector and Supabase Auth this tier introduces.
